item.title: “But when is International Iguana’s Day?” asks unbearably tedious iguana
item.description: It’s International Women’s Day on Sunday. Many people will enjoy the annual celebration, but there are some who feel that dedicating a single day dedicated to women is some sort of affront, including an unbearably tedious iguana, who has taken to social media to protest.

item.title: Clacton to build Mar-a-Lago replica in hope of attracting occasional visit from Nigel Farage
item.description: Residents of Clacton-on-Sea have unveiled ambitious plans to construct a full-scale replica of Mar-a-Lago in a desperate bid to lure their MP, Nigel Farage, back to the constituency for anything other than a fleeting visit for a couple of selfies. item.title: Confused Trump claims Saddam Hussein building weapons of mass destruction
item.description: A confused Donald Trump has claimed Saddam Hussein is building weapons of mass destruction, it has been revealed.

item.title: UK strangely reluctant to follow an adjudicated sexual abuser and convicted felon into another illegal war
item.description: The United Kingdom has reacted with what Washington insiders describe as “deeply unhelpful hesitation” after the United States and Israel began attacking Iran, with Britain apparently unwilling to immediately follow an adjudicated sexual abuser and convicted felon into yet another illegal war.

item.title: Reform calls for new law to replace International Women’s Day with British Women’s Day
item.description: Reform UK have demanded that the UK no longer recognise International Women’s Day and should instead celebrate British Women’s Day.

item.title: Nationwide now offering 30-year mortgages for 1st Class Stamps
item.description: Nationwide Building Society has extended its range of mortgages for postage stamps to 30 years, after Royal Mail’s latest price rises made them unaffordable over the usual 25.

item.title: White smoke rising from Tehran signals they’ve just chosen or just lost a new Supreme Leader
item.description: A new column of billowing smoke seen in Tehran is believed to signify the end of the selection process for the new Supreme Leader, or possibly just the end of the new Supreme Leader.

item.title: Canine eugenics tournament hailed as massive success
item.description: A four-year-old clumber spaniel has won Best In Show at Crufts, the annual tournament for those with a strong interest in the practice of eugenics.

item.title: Quentin Tarantino begins auditioning feet for West End debut
item.description: Filmmaker Quentin Tarantino has begun the process of casting feet for his upcoming play on the West End, it has been revealed.
